Library

Contributing

This is the author's personal collection, open to conversation and reusable contributions. Self-authored Skills, philosopher recommendations, tool introductions and discussions, philosophical arguments, and practical improvements are welcome. Agreement with Yinyang's philosophy is not a condition of participation. Explain the relation you want to examine or change so others can assess and continue the work.

Create independently, develop your version, or contribute here

You may take inspiration from the form of making philosophy usable and create entirely different content, organization, and tools in your own repository. You need not retain Yinyang, join this collection, fork this repository, or open an Issue first. An independent work may express a different or opposing philosophy; its existence does not depend on this maintainer's agreement.

You may also copy or fork existing material under its applicable license and add philosophy, arguments, examples, criticism, rigor, or technical realization in your own version. Your own philosophy belongs in your own repository; share a link through an Issue rather than proposing its inclusion in this collection. The Issue/PR workflow below applies only to questions and changes you want to bring into this repository.

References to relevant material and acknowledgments of inspiration are welcome, as is returning with a new work for conversation and mutual introductions through links or mutual mentions in relevant discussions. Independent works determine licensing from their own sources and rights; reuse of this repository's material follows that material's attribution and license requirements. Permission to create or modify, source attribution, and whether this repository accepts a merge are different questions. LICENSING.md describes the licensing scope.

Contributing here: Issue or pull request?

Self-authored reusable Skills and improvements to existing Skills or tools can be submitted directly as PRs. Explain their purpose, use, and observed results. The public formation guides and methods for organizing, using, and revising Yinyang's six working files are also open to PRs; each person's private accounts and sources stay private. These contributions do not require agreement with the author's philosophy. For philosophy, create your own work in your own repository. Share it, recommend philosophers, discuss tools, or question this collection's arguments through Issues. The author retains authorship and revision of this philosophical collection; it is not a shared repository for other authors' essays.

PRs are also welcome for clear additional improvements, translations into other languages, and adaptations for other agent harnesses, CLIs, or applications, such as Claude Code. Contributors can extend the work beyond the environment the author maintains. Explain the concrete benefit, the actual target and entrypoint, what you tried there, and any remaining limitations. A portable method and a verified working adaptation establish different contributions; describe the one the PR supplies. Preserve the source meaning and relevant consumer boundaries while adapting its realization.

Discussion and contributions can concern philosophy, personal-modeling methods, tools, and singing, through the routes above. Model-making methods and sanitized examples are welcome; another person's private portrait is not public contribution material. The singing station welcomes song requests and proposed recordings through its comments or a GitHub Issue. Include the song title, performer credit, an accessible recording link, and the permission that allows publication. Contributors may also propose a PR with a recording catalog entry; the native website owner integrates accepted entries into content/singing/recordings.json and publishes the player. Each entry supplies title, performer, audio_url, source_url, and rights. This is an invitation to contribute, not an automatic upload or blanket license for recordings.

What you have Where to start What to include
A question, unclear passage, objection, or missing reference Open an Issue Link the page or file, identify the passage, and explain the question or competing interpretation. Include sources when a factual claim depends on them.
A broken page, tool, link, or installation Open an Issue Describe what you tried, what you expected, and what happened. Add the relevant environment and a minimal example or screenshot when useful.
Your own philosophy, a philosopher recommendation, a tool introduction, or related discussion Open an Issue Share a link or explain the relevant idea. Maintain your independent philosophy in your own repository.
A reusable Skill, a concrete improvement, a translation or harness adaptation, or a better method for the six working files Open a PR directly Explain its purpose, use, result, and checks. A prior Issue is optional; exclude private accounts and source material.
A change to this repository's overall direction or a broad reorganization proposed for merging Open an Issue for discussion first State the purpose, proposed scope, alternatives, and effect on existing users. A new self-authored Skill does not require this preliminary step merely because it is new. This does not restrict your independent version.

Use Chinese or English for discussion. A short, concrete description is enough; you do not need a finished theory or implementation specification to ask a question. Related discussion can continue in one Issue instead of opening a new one for every reply.

Preparing a change for this repository

Fork the repository, make a branch for the change, and open a pull request against main. Keep one coherent purpose in a PR. Link an existing Issue when there is one, but do not create an Issue solely to satisfy a template.

Read the affected package's instructions. AGENTS.md and MODEL.md explain source ownership; each Skill may add its own maintenance guidance. Edit original material at its owner and preserve the meaning of both English and Chinese reader editions. If you can update only one language, state the translation gap clearly so it can be resolved during review.

The website/ directory is a generated snapshot of the native Site source. For website changes, an Issue can identify the desired result, or a PR can provide a proposed patch to the snapshot. Mark it as a website proposal: the maintainer will apply the accepted change at the native source, regenerate the snapshot, and publish it. Direct edits to generated copies do not become a second maintenance source. Canonical Yinyang writing belongs in skills/yinyang/.

What reviewers need

  • The concrete problem or purpose and the behavior or meaning after the change.
  • Relevant sources for factual corrections, with interpretation distinguished from quotation or established results.
  • Appropriate checks: readable links and language parity for text; a useful real example for a Skill or script; screenshots for layout changes; relevant build or behavior checks for implementation changes.
  • Any remaining uncertainty, translation gap, or check you could not perform.

Scale checking to the change. A wording correction does not need a new test suite. AI assistance is welcome; the submitter remains responsible for reading the proposed changes, checking their claims, and excluding private material.

Public material and rights

Issues and PRs are public. Remove credentials, private conversations, personal portraits, and material you are not authorized to publish. Use a minimal, sanitized example when reporting a problem. Do not paste a secret into an Issue.

Contributions follow the existing license of the affected material; this does not relicense unrelated work. Yinyang's original material uses CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, and the other reusable Skill packages use their included MIT licenses. Retain attribution and third-party notices and identify outside sources. LICENSING.md records the scope.

Review may request a clarification, revision, or narrower scope. The maintainer handles merging and publication; opening an Issue or PR does not guarantee adoption. Discuss arguments and observable effects, leaving room for independent works and other ways of using the shared material.
